front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《1》

zh: 詩有自己的軌道和方向
en: Or quietly listening to the footsteps of the fog
Or counting the light of the stars one by one
A poem has its own orbit and direction

zh: 齊柏林 : 國在山河破
《看見台灣》: 島嶼的美麗和哀愁
en: Du Fu: the nation broken, yet its rivers and mountains remain
Chi Po-lin: the nation stands, but its mountains and rivers lie broken
"Beyond Beauty: Taiwan from Above": the beauty and sorrow of the island

points.zh:
國破山河在，城春草木深。
感時花濺淚，恨別鳥驚心。
烽火連三月，家書抵萬金。
白頭搔更短，渾欲不勝簪。
--唐。杜甫。《 春望 》
齊柏林 : 影片《看見台灣》---歷時5年，累積400小時直升機空拍視野。第50屆金馬獎最佳記錄片，2013。 6/10/2017，空中拍攝《看見台灣 2》影像集時，墜機罹難於花蓮山海交接處。
齊柏林。《 從空中看台灣—攝影集 》。 2006
序言 : 「 直到十多年的現在，當我在機上驚喜地瞥見台灣美麗的小小角落，我仍興奮得直覺此生無憾。只不過，這份感動不再那麼純粹了，摻雜著一絲遺憾和危機感，甚至淡淡悲傷。環境相扣的自然條件和人爲活動形塑了台灣多樣化的面貎，有的美得不可方物，有的醜陋得禁不起細看。老實說，近年來眼中所見，相較於令人喜悅的場景，台灣敎我失望的比例高出甚多。這個嚴厲的事實或許要讓讀者失望了，但卻讓我意識到，自己不僅扮演創作者的角色，同時更是個記錄者。《從空中看台灣》不只是齊柏林的個人作品，也是生活在台灣的你我共同譜寫的史詩，無論它是好是壞，我們都不能否定自己參與了這塊土地的創作程。也許，有幾幅照片讓你怦然心動，有幾幅讓你掩卷沉思，不管這本書激發何種心緒，我卑微地希望，讀者們能和我一起享受飛行的樂趣，并從中找到值得自己奮鬥的目標和理由，不吝惜在生活中做一些舉手之勞，讓這塊土地變得更加美好。」
「很多人都會在口頭上說愛台灣，其實并不瞭解這塊土地，我希望能透過影像，讓大家首先認識台灣，然後呵護台灣。」
「換個高度，看得更清楚」
「換個態度，善待自己，善待自然」
齊柏林去了，他成爲愛台灣聽其言，觀其行的典範。而這方土地也呼喚更多的齊柏林，用一顆透明和天真的心，用心靈的鏡頭，繼續記錄著這片生生不息的土地 。
points.en:
The state is broken, though mountains and rivers remain; spring comes to the city, and grass and trees grow deep.
Grieving over the times, even the flowers seem to weep; hating parting, even birds startle the heart.
The beacon fires have continued for three months; a letter from home would be worth ten thousand pieces of gold.
My white hair, from scratching, has grown ever thinner; it can hardly even hold a hairpin.
-- Tang Dynasty. Du Fu. "Spring View" (春望)
Chi Po-lin: the film "Beyond Beauty: Taiwan from Above" (看見台灣) — five years in the making, accumulating 400 hours of helicopter aerial footage. Winner of Best Documentary Feature at the 50th Golden Horse Awards, 2013. On June 10, 2017, while filming aerial footage for "Beyond Beauty: Taiwan from Above 2," he died in a helicopter crash where the mountains meet the sea in Hualien.
Chi Po-lin. "Taiwan from the Air — A Photography Collection" (從空中看台灣—攝影集). 2006.
Preface: "Even now, more than a decade later, when I glimpse from the plane some small, beautiful corner of Taiwan, I still feel instinctively that I could die without regret. Only, this feeling of being moved is no longer so pure — it is now mixed with a trace of regret, a sense of crisis, even a faint sadness. The interlocking natural conditions and human activity have shaped Taiwan's diverse face — some of it beautiful beyond compare, some of it too ugly to bear close scrutiny. Honestly, in recent years, compared to the joyful scenes, the proportion of scenes that have disappointed me in Taiwan has been much greater. This harsh truth may disappoint readers, but it has made me realize that I am not only a creator, but even more a recorder. 'Taiwan from the Air' is not only Chi Po-lin's personal work, but also an epic co-authored by all of us who live in Taiwan — whether it is good or bad, none of us can deny that we have taken part in the making of this land. Perhaps some photographs will move your heart, and others will make you close the book and sit in thought; whatever feelings this book stirs, I humbly hope that readers will join me in enjoying the pleasure of flight, and find in it goals and reasons worth striving for, and will not begrudge small efforts in daily life that make this land a better place."
"Many people say they love Taiwan, but in truth do not understand this land. I hope that through images, everyone can first come to know Taiwan, and then cherish and protect it."
"Change your altitude, and see more clearly."
"Change your attitude — treat yourself well, and treat nature well."
Chi Po-lin has passed, but he has become a model of one who loved Taiwan not merely in words but in deeds. And this land calls for more Chi Po-lins, to continue recording this ever-living land with a transparent and innocent heart, through the lens of the soul.

en: Recalling the evening glow of those years
A painted scroll
Every brushstroke leaves blank space for you
AlphaGo,  go,  go,  go
You take your sunlit highway
I cross my own log bridge

points.zh: 5/27/2017，谷歌人工智慧系統AlphaGo，對戰中國圍棋棋王柯潔取得3連勝。「AlphaGo之父」哈薩比斯賽後表示，這是AlphaGo參加的最後對弈比賽，從此退役。其棋藝已遠遠超過九段棋力，人類無以超越。AlphaGo只花二年時間就達到目前的實力。
points.en: On May 27, 2017, Google's artificial intelligence system AlphaGo achieved three consecutive victories against China's top Go player Ke Jie. After the match, Demis Hassabis, "the father of AlphaGo," stated that this was AlphaGo's final competitive match, after which it would retire. Its playing skill had already far surpassed nine-dan level, beyond what humans could match. AlphaGo took only two years to reach its current level of ability.

zh: 那是暮春最美的薫衣草
en: That is the most beautiful lavender of late spring
Waves of poetry drift on the wind
Waiting to be interpreted

zh: 「 最近好嗎 ?  都想些什麼 ?」
en: "How have you been lately? What's been on your mind?"
Black  Hole,  Dark  Matter,  Supernova...
Going far off to form a universe of its own

zh: 坐在現代的風景看古代的風景
en: Sitting in a modern landscape, watching an ancient one
So spoke Homer
So said Sima Qian

points.zh: 荷馬是希臘瞎眼的吟唱詩人， 留下二部古希臘文學經典《荷馬史詩》 : 伊里亞德和奧德賽。叙述海倫--木馬的特洛伊戰爭以及奧德賽和水手十年海上漂泊的歷險記。
points.en: Homer was the blind bard of ancient Greece who left behind two classics of ancient Greek literature, the Homeric epics: the Iliad and the Odyssey — recounting the Trojan War fought over Helen and the wooden horse, and Odysseus's decade-long ordeal of wandering the seas with his sailors.

points.zh: 司馬遷是受宮刑的西漢史學家和文學家，他撰寫的《史記》被公認是中國史書的典範。被後世尊稱為史遷。其史學觀念在於“ 究天人之際，通古今之變，成一家之言 ”。

en: The fog has cleared
Above the landscape
Hanging there, a drunken sunset
From then, that drop of rain
Then stay within the palm of my hand
Waiting for childhood's dragonfly to fly back

zh: 杜甫，你也來阿里山看雲海
en: I will ascend to the very summit
At a glance, all the mountains grow small
Du Fu, you too have come to Ali Mountain to watch the sea of clouds

points.zh:
岱宗夫如何，齊魯青未了。
造化鍾神秀，隂陽割昏曉。
蕩胸生層雲，決眦入歸鳥。
會當凌絕頂，一覽衆山小。
--唐。杜甫。《望岳》
points.en:
How is it with Mount Tai? Its green stretches unending across Qi and Lu.
Creation and Nature concentrated their divine splendor here; yin and yang divide dusk from dawn.
Rising clouds stir the breast; returning birds enter eyes strained wide open.
I shall surely climb to the very summit, and see all the other mountains grow small.
-- Tang dynasty. Du Fu, 'Gazing at the Sacred Mountain' (Wang Yue)
